newsitem.title: UK: Tight security for Prince Charles in N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Tight security for Prince Charles in N.Ireland.

text.p: Prince Charles paid a high security visit to Northern Ireland on Tuesday, his first since Irish guerrillas stepped up a war on troops and police in the British-ruled province late last year.
The heir to the British throne was greeted warmly when he visited two Protestant districts, in the town of Carrickfergus and in south Belfast, where support for British rule is strong.
Later he was due to open Belfast's showpiece 32 million pound ($52 million) Waterfront Hall by the banks of the River Lagan before a gala concert featuring opera singer Kiri Te Kanawa.

The outlawed Irish Republican Army, fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, abandoned a 17-month truce in February 1996 and detonated a series of bombs in London. In October the IRA launched a wave of attacks in Northern Ireland and has killed two soldiers since then.
Charles has been a target of protests on previous trips to both sides of the divided island because he holds the largely ceremonial title of "colonel-in-chief" of the elite Parachute Regiment.
Paratroops shot dead 13 unarmed Irish nationalists during a Roman Catholic protest march in Londonderry city in 1972 in what became known as "Bloody Sunday".
Northern Ireland's Catholic minority say Britain should reopen an investigation into the killings and formally declare the victims innocent. ($1=.6136 Pound)
